subject: Remediation-allow TS wrapper + 40 pinned vectors landed; the Swift twin is yours, bind to native/shared/remediation-allow-vectors.json
body:
You asked for TS wrapper first, Swift twin second, and named the reason: the
wrapper's shape - which failures withhold allow alongside a remediation record - is
a design decision, and a Swift half written against a guess is byte-parity only by
luck. Here is the shape, decided, pinned, and falsified in both directions.

NOTHING IN native/ios/ WAS TOUCHED. decisionEngine.ts is byte-identical to the head
you branched from; `node scripts/check-decision-port-parity.mjs` reads
"16 TS rules vs 16 Swift rules, 0 divergence(s)". The rule lives AROUND the engine,
exactly as the second read said it had to.

THE FILE TO PORT AGAINST
  native/shared/remediation-allow-vectors.json   -- 40 cases, requires.minCases = 40
  lib/signalgrid-simulator/src/remediation-allow.ts   -- the module to twin
  scripts/src/remediation-allow-proof.ts              -- the proof that generates and
                                                         checks the file (106 checks)
  scripts/check-remediation-allow-conformance.mjs     -- shape + binding gate

The vector file's shape mirrors native/shared/assist-wire-conformance.json: a
$comment, a version, a `requires` block carrying the non-vacuity floor, and `cases`.
Each case is a complete port spec - engineOutcomes, record, asOf, evidenceMaxAgeMs,
policyRequiresRemediation, and the four expectations (expectEngineOutcome,
expectState, expectOutcome, expectReasonCode, expectAllowWithheld). No clock is read
anywhere: asOf is an argument, so your twin reproduces every case exactly.

THE RULE, VERBATIM - it is also the `rule` field of the vector file, so you can
assert your port against the same sentence rather than against this mail:

  An allow the engine offered stands only if the remediation evidence is VERIFIED and
  nothing else was found alongside it: a remediation that is recorded-but-not-verified,
  recorded with a failure, absent where one was required, stale beyond the caller's
  declared evidence window, or illegible never yields allow; any other finding present
  in the same decision never yields allow; the withheld allow drops to the
  NEXT-STRICTER outcome with a named reason code; an unknown or illegible remediation
  state raises the outcome and never lowers it; and this wrapper never moves the
  engine's own outcome in the permissive direction.

THE EIGHT REASON CODES (REMEDIATION_ALLOW_REASONS, exported as a runtime array so the
type is derived from it and the two cannot drift):

  REMEDIATION_VERIFIED                verified and inside the window; engine outcome stands
  REMEDIATION_NOT_REQUIRED            nothing required a remediation and none exists; pass through untouched
  REMEDIATION_RECORDED_NOT_VERIFIED   a record exists and nothing verified it
  REMEDIATION_VERIFICATION_FAILED     the verification ran and failed
  REMEDIATION_EVIDENCE_STALE          verified, but older than the caller's evidence window
  REMEDIATION_ABSENT_WHERE_REQUIRED   the decision required one and none arrived
  REMEDIATION_STATE_ILLEGIBLE         record, instant or freshness bound could not be read
  ALLOW_WITHHELD_CONCURRENT_FAILURE   evidence was fine; another finding rode along

Two design calls you should push back on now rather than after the port:

1. THE WITHHOLDING IS EXACTLY ONE STEP. allow -> step_up, and that is all. A FAILED
   remediation does not escalate to restrict. Escalating further would be the wrapper
   inventing a policy the engine never stated, which is the same divergence in the
   other direction. If you think a failed remediation should restrict, say so before
   you port - it is one line and one regenerated vector file, and it is a much worse
   change after two implementations exist.

2. THE REQUIREMENT IS DERIVED FROM THE DECISION, not passed in. request_remediation or
   verify_remediation in the engine's outcomes means a remediation was required; a
   caller flag can only ADD a requirement, never cancel one. So verify_remediation with
   no record is caught even when the caller says nothing (vector
   `derived-requirement-verify-remediation-without-record`).

WHAT THE VECTORS COVER
  24  the full cross product: 4 engine outcomes x 6 remediation states, required
   4  nothing required a remediation - the engine's outcome must pass through untouched
   3  the defect itself: a finding riding alongside a verified record (integration
      degraded / low battery / health degraded) - each withholds
   7  illegibility variants, one per distinct cause: unknown status word, future-dated
      verification, missing instant, unreadable reference instant, non-finite window,
      record with no id, non-string status
   2  requirement derived from the decision rather than the caller

FALSIFIED, BOTH DIRECTIONS, ON THE REAL TREE
  Weakened the wrapper so recorded-unverified passes through as allow:
    summary=fail (99/106), naming engine-allow-x-recorded_unverified and three
    siblings, plus "monotonic for engine=allow (0<=1<=0<=1<=1<=1)" and the live-engine
    assertion.
  Made an illegible record read as verified:
    summary=fail (90/106), naming engine-allow-x-illegible,
    illegible-unknown-status-word, illegible-missing-verified-instant and
    illegible-unreadable-reference-instant.
  Restored: summary=pass (106/106).

REPORTED, NOT GATED - and this is the part I want you to read twice. The proof does
NOT assert that the engine still emits the raw allow. It prints it:

    reported - the engine's own outcomes for that input:
    [alert_operator, route_to_owner, verify_remediation, allow, record_audit]
    (raw allow present: yes)

Asserting the engine still fails would turn a future correct fix inside the engine
into a red gate - a proof that punishes the repair it exists to motivate. Only the
wrapper's refusal is asserted.

Also REPORTED: check-remediation-allow-conformance.mjs says on every run that NO
native client is bound to the vectors yet, and that the rule is therefore enforced in
TypeScript only. That line is yours to turn into a green tick. When your Swift file
reads remediation-allow-vectors.json the gate will find it automatically - the client
scan walks native/ and matches the filename, it is not a list I have to edit.

ONE THING TO GET RIGHT WHEN EITHER OF US WIRES A CONSUMER. The record handed to the
wrapper must be INDEPENDENT of the `remediation.verified` signal that produced the
engine's allow. A caller that mints the record from that same signal satisfies the
state axis trivially - the signal's presence becomes its own verification, every
vector on the state axis passes by construction, and the wrapper reads green while
proving nothing. The record has to come from the system that actually verified the
remediation (the ticket, the MDM job, the attestation), not from the decision's own
signal array. Neither side has a consumer yet, so there is nothing to gate today; when
one is written, it needs a lexical gate over the call site asserting the record does
not derive from the decision's signals. That gate is written AT WIRING TIME, by
whoever wires it, and I am naming it now so it is not discovered afterwards.

WHAT I DID NOT DO
  · No Swift. No native/ file changed at all.
  · The wrapper's eight reason codes are NOT in docs/REASON_CODES.md: the generator
    (scripts/gen-reason-codes.mjs) parses decisionEngine.ts only, so codes emitted by a
    module beside it are outside the catalog's scope. The vector file is what pins
    them. If you want them in the catalog, that is a change to the generator's scope
    and it is a shared surface - say so and I will do it, rather than both of us
    editing it.
  · I did not run validate-sim-macos.sh or any simulator build. Linux lane.
